metadata.title: Attributions & Scholarly Citations
metadata.description: Primary academic and computational sources powering the Urdu Meter Handbook and Interactive Studio.

entries.title: Urdu Meter: A Practical Handbook
entries.urdu_title: اردو بحور: ایک عملی دستی کتاب
entries.publisher_or_affiliation: Department of Middle Eastern, South Asian, and African Studies (MESAAS), Columbia University; South Asian Studies, University of Wisconsin-Madison
entries.summary: The primary intellectual, theoretical, and pedagogical foundation of this software. Pritchett & Khaliq formulated the empirical weight rule ('2 letters = Long (=), 1 letter = Short (-)'), the vertical syllable code-breaking scansion method, the catalog of 37 classical meters grouped into melodic families, the rules of flexibility (x), and the 24 classical ghazal exercises with answer keys.
entries.related_project: Also citing Frances W. Pritchett's monumental online research repository 'A Desertful of Roses: The Divan of Ghalib in Urdu with Complete Scansions and Commentary' (https://franpritchett.com/00ghalib/).

entries.title: Bah'r: The Backbone of Shaayari
entries.urdu_title: بحر: شاعری کی ریڑھ کی ہڈی
entries.summary: A widely-shared plain-language introduction to bah'r, teaching 13 of the most popular bah'rs (each with its arkaan/afa'il and an illustrative sher plus a classic couplet by a named ustaad) via the ghazal community's own ASCII romanization rather than academic transliteration. This app cross-references its 13 named bah'rs against Pritchett's 37-meter catalog (12 of the 13 match cleanly; the 13th, a 4-foot 'Mutadaarik Saalim', is a shortened usage of catalog meter #12 rather than a distinct meter) and folds 11 of its classic couplets in as extra examples on the matching meters in Meter › Lookup. See data/urdupoetry_bahrs.json for the full extraction, meter mapping, and scan verification, and docs/reviews/18-urdupoetry-bahrs.md for the write-up.
entries.related_project: Saved locally at data/sources/urdupoetry_art5.html so the extraction is reproducible.

entries.title: Finite-State AST Graph Transliteration & Multi-Script Parsing Engine (ghalib.js)
entries.urdu_title: محدود المعطیات گراف پر مبنی کثیر الخطی ٹرانسلٹریشن انجن
entries.publisher_or_affiliation: Department of Linguistics, Languages, and Cultures, Michigan State University; Columbia University South Asian Digital Humanities
entries.summary: Developer of the underlying finite-state transition graph and abstract syntax tree parser ('ghalib.js', 'urdu_parser_data.js', 'devanagari_parser_data.js', 'diacritics_parser_data.js') originally installed in October 2002 on Columbia's 'A Desertful of Roses'. In this application, Sean Pue's algorithm powers our multi-script engine, enabling instantaneous switching across Urdu Nastaliq, Devanagari, Roman with academic diacritics, and ASCII.
